personality_one_liner: A vibrant, approachable, and highly tactile study companion that makes mastering sonography feel encouraging and manageable.

spacing.rule: Generous padding around chunky cards, prominent thumb-zones for CTAs. Let the empty space highlight the learning material.

do's: Use on sticky submit button container during quizzes
dont's: Do not use on standard list rows

screens.name: Home
screens.purpose: Dashboard to select the 5 sonography topics, view quick progress, and access bookmarks.

states.empty: No recent activity, start a topic! with a playful illustration.
states.error: Failed to load progress, Retry button

screens.layout: Top section: Toggle for Dark/Light mode and Welcome message. Middle: Grid/List of 5 chunky cards (Overview, Liver, Gallbladder, Pancreas, GI Tract) utilizing their respective topic accent colors (brandTertiary-like backgrounds). Bottom: Quick stats (overall completion %).

screens.name: Topic Notes
screens.purpose: Read study notes and mnemonics for a selected topic.
screens.layout: Sticky glass header with Topic Title and Bookmark action. Scrollable body text with generous line-height. Mnemonics presented in distinct, tinted pill-shaped callout blocks. Large text for easy reading.

screens.name: Flashcards
screens.purpose: Interactive study via tap-to-flip or swipeable cards.

states.empty: You've reviewed all cards! Reset deck button.

screens.layout: Single prominent card centered on screen with heavy shadow (tier 2) and large radius. Tap to flip (animated via reanimated). Bottom sticky area with two large pill buttons: 'Learning' (warning color) and 'Known' (success color). A progress bar pinned to the top.

screens.name: MCQ Quiz
screens.layout: Question text at the top. 4 chunky tile-based options stacked vertically. Tapping an option highlights it (borderStrong or brand tint). Sticky primary 'Submit' button at the bottom (thumb zone). Upon submission, a bottom sheet slides up showing the explanation and 'Next Question' button.

screens.name: Progress Dashboard
screens.purpose: Track learning statistics and overall completion.

states.empty: Start studying to see your progress!

screens.layout: Modular card-based system. Top: Overall completion circular progress or thick bar. Middle: Streak counter and recent quiz scores. Bottom: List of bookmarked notes or flashcards for quick resume.

quiz_success.alt: Silhouette of a person celebrating success against a sunset

study_empty.alt: White paper on a white surface representing study materials

instructions_to_main_agent: CRITICAL: The app must support both Light and Dark mode using the provided nested 'light' and 'dark' tokens in the color block. Implement an explicit in-app toggle (e.g., in the Home header or a Settings tab).
Use AsyncStorage or SQLite to save all user data locally: progress, flashcard states (known/learning), quiz scores, and bookmarks. Do NOT implement any backend or cloud syncing.

Utilize the 5 provided per-topic accent colors (topicOverview, topicLiver, etc.) to visually distinguish the 5 topics. Tint the topic cards on the Home screen and the callout backgrounds in the Topic Notes screen.
Implement the 'Tactile / Playful' visual style: use chunky cards with large border radii (lg/pill), prominent shadows (tier 2), and oversized touch targets.
For Flashcards, implement a flip animation using react-native-reanimated. Include 'Learning' and 'Known' actions that save the state locally and advance the deck.
For MCQ Quizzes, use tile-based selectable options and a sticky submit button anchored at the bottom (thumb-zone). Show explanations seamlessly in a @gorhom/bottom-sheet.
Mnemonics inside the Study Notes should stand out significantly—wrap them in visually distinct, tinted containers using the topic accent or brandTertiary, paired with a matching icon.
Ensure 'Nunito' is used for body text and 'Fredoka' for display headings, keeping font weights to a maximum of 500.
Apply 'expo-blur' (glass effect) to the bottom tab bar and any sticky headers covering scrollable content. Ensure foreground text over glass maintains high contrast.
